Job Description And Duties

The Research Data Specialist I (RDS I) independently performs technical research and statistical work, with primary responsibility for business intelligence reporting, Power BI development, data visualization, and developing and maintaining data models and reporting solutions for the Department of Developmental Services (Department), Employment Services and other programs. Responsibilities include complex statistical data generation, manipulation, analysis, and reporting to support program oversight and data-driven decision making. The incumbent also serves as a technical resource to staff on program statistics, reporting methodologies, and data interpretation.

Effective July 1, 2025, State employees are subject to a salary reduction of three percent in exchange for five hours per month of the Personal Leave.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Working Conditions

Under Government Code 14200, this position is a hybrid, in-office/telework position, and may be subject to change. Incumbent can be required to report to the office, or any designated location at any time. Telework agreements can be modified and/or cancelled at any time.

Pursuant to California Government Code requirements, candidates must be residents of the State of California at the time of appointment. All commute expenses to the reporting location will be the responsibility of the selected candidate.

This position requires lawful authorization to work in the United States. The Department does not sponsor employment visas for this position.

The position requires the incumbent to maintain consistent and regular attendance, communicate effectively while working with the public, community members, management, staff, and control agencies; develop and maintain knowledge and skills related to specific tasks, methodologies, materials, tools and equipment; complete assignments in a timely and efficient manner; and adhere to departmental policies and procedures.

Services are provided through state-operated developmental centers and community facilities, and contracts with 21 nonprofit regional centers. The regional centers serve as a local resource to help find and access the services and supports available to individuals with developmental disabilities and their families.

jobs.title: Communications and Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Please see “How to Apply” below. Candidates who email a personalized cover letter will be prioritized for review.

The Center for Ecoliteracy is seeking a Communications and Program Coordinator to join our small and dynamic team that includes educators, former school nutrition professionals, food systems experts, advocates, and parents.

About this Role

The Communications and Program Coordinator supports the organization’s mission by coordinating program activities and translating those efforts into compelling digital communications that engage participants, partners, and broader audiences. 

This is a key role on our team that will advance the Center for Ecoliteracy’s California Food for California Kids® initiative. The Communications and Program Coordinator will build relationships with school nutrition leaders across California, help shape the statewide conversation on transforming school food, experience and document stories of innovative farm to school programs, and contribute to policy and systems change that benefits millions of students.

This position reports to the Program Manager of the California Food for California Kids® initiative and is a full-time, exempt position. 

Who We Are Seeking 

You are a thoughtful communicator with a collaborative spirit. You keep a pulse on new communications platforms and technology. Meeting new people and picking up the phone gives you energy and inspiration. You prioritize authentic relationships over outcomes. You enjoy translating complex ideas into clear, engaging content and are skilled at managing multiple projects and platforms. Technology is your friend – you’re a problem-solver when it comes to tech glitches and hiccups. You are excited to support a mission-driven team working to create a more equitable and sustainable school food system. You love food and the culture surrounding it, with a deep appreciation for the people who grow and prepare it, as well as the community they serve. You are proactive, detail-oriented, and ready to dive in and contribute meaningfully to a small, high-impact organization.

Our Workplace Culture

The Center for Ecoliteracy supports a culture that prioritizes integrity, high professional standards, and working successfully with diverse colleagues, program beneficiaries, and community partners. This includes active participation in promoting a healthy workplace culture through organizational diversity and program assessment for equity and inclusion. We strive to build a culture of cooperation and mutual support and value flexibility, resilience, optimism, curiosity, and a sense of shared purpose.

Responsibilities

Lead digital communications across video, websites, webinars, email campaigns, and social media platforms. Generate compelling content, including short-form videos, graphics, and photography that engage program beneficiaries, donors, and partners.
Support the development of comprehensive communication plans to effectively disseminate new resources, event opportunities, and other program offerings. Liaise with partner organizations to coordinate cross-promotion and resource dissemination.
Support the coordination of photo and video shoots at schools, farms, and events throughout California. Provide on-site support for vendors and program participants to ensure a positive, meaningful experience.
Track and analyze digital metrics to inform communication strategies.
Maintain a brand asset library (graphics, photos, and video), and support the team in using assets correctly.
Support our programs by hosting and facilitating conferences, events, and webinars; coordinating event logistics; and managing outreach, recruitment, promotion, registration, and contact lists. Conduct research and develop prep materials to provide a seamless experience for staff and participants.
Contribute to program evaluation and reporting by gathering data and tracking project outcomes. Lead systems for tracking and managing relationships with school nutrition professionals and educators. 
Represent the organization and engage with school nutrition professionals, educators, students, policymakers, and nonprofit and state agency partners at conferences, events, webinars, and visits to schools and farms.

Required Skills and Experience

Minimum 2–3 years of experience in communications, marketing, journalism, or a related field.
Excellent project management skills. Thrives managing multiple deadlines in a fast-paced, collaborative environment while delivering a high standard of excellence.
Experience with event planning and coordination. Comfortable pivoting from detailed execution to strategic decision-making under pressure. 
Comfort engaging with external partners and representing the organization.
Ability to build and use spreadsheets to manage program data, synthesize project outcomes, and communicate impact to staff. 
Strong writing and editing skills, with attention to detail and storytelling.
Proficiency in digital platforms, including social media, email marketing tools, and web content management systems. The Center for Ecoliteracy works in an Apple environment and uses Adobe Creative Cloud, Drupal, Mailchimp, Hootsuite, Zoom, Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Threads, Slack, Dropbox, Canva, and Google Workspace.
Proficiency in best practices for digital design, such as editing, cropping, and ensuring correct file types for different platforms.  
Experience tailoring content for various audiences, such as school nutrition professionals, educators, donors, policymakers, or California families.

Preferred Skills and Experience

Experience working with nonprofit organizations or public school nutrition programs.
Familiarity with food systems, education, or advocacy campaigns.
Spanish language fluency is a plus.

Location and Travel

The Center for Ecoliteracy has a hybrid work environment in the landmark David Brower Center in Downtown Berkeley, California. This role follows a hybrid schedule (in-office on Tuesday and Thursday, remote on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday) and requires regular travel to support events, storytelling, and other engagements within California.

Salary

This is a full-time, exempt position. The salary is based on experience and ranges from $80,000 to $85,000 annually. A comprehensive benefits package is included.

How to Apply

Please email a brief cover letter, three relevant work samples, and your resume to jobs@ecoliteracy.org with the subject line “[Last Name, First Name]: Communications and Program Coordinator Application.” Interviews will be conducted in August 2026.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Center for Ecoliteracy is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, or disability.

Our Commitment to Equity and Racial Justice

The Center for Ecoliteracy pursues change in TK–12 education and school food systems to provide a more just, sustainable, and equitable experience for students and the people who nourish them. We recognize the harm that systemic racism, gender bias, and structural inequalities create in our public education, food, and labor systems, and strive to mitigate the health and educational inequities affecting low-income households and children of color. We amplify the voices of people who are marginalized and shape our work according to their messages. By listening and taking action to identify and include missing voices, we seek to shift power in both policy and decision-making. We are privileged to learn from our partners and will continue to grow and evolve our work to embody this commitment.

About the Center for Ecoliteracy

The Center for Ecoliteracy is reimagining school food as a pathway for learning and change.
For 30 years, we’ve transformed education in classrooms, cafeterias, and gardens—partnering with hundreds of school districts, supporting thousands of educators, and ensuring millions of children have access to nutritious meals at school.

Our core initiative, California Food for California Kids®, inspires schools to serve fresh, locally-sourced meals and engage students in the connections between food, culture, health, and the environment.
Together, we can build a healthier, more hopeful future for our children.

Learn more at ecoliteracy.org.

AI-Native Global Trade & Tariff Management | Recognized in the 2025 Gartner® Market Guide
Customer Success Data Analyst – Implementation & Execution

Full-Time | Hybrid Irvine, CA/Remote | US Based
——————————————————————————————————————————
About KYG Trade™ KYG Trade™ is an AI-native, enterprise-grade Global Trade and Tariff Management (GTM²) platform that turns trade compliance complexity into clarity. Recognized in the 2025 Gartner® Market Guide for Global Trade Management, KYG Trade™ delivers expert-trained AI across import and export compliance, tariff optimization, forced labor/UFLPA, FTA qualification, restricted party screening, and supply chain ESG traceability — all on a single platform.d
KYG Trade™ integrates with enterprise ecosystems including SAP ECC, SAP S/4HANA, SAP GTS, Oracle ERP, Windchill, and other leading ERP, PLM, TMS, and risk systems, enabling customers to deploy trade controls and workflow automation in complex global environments.
The Role The Customer Success Data Analyst – Implementation & Execution will support KYG Trade™ customer onboarding, implementation, and adoption by owning critical data analysis, data readiness, reporting, configuration support, and customer-facing execution activities across the Customer Success organization.
This role is designed for someone who can operate at the intersection of data analysis, SaaS implementation, customer success, and trade compliance operations. The analyst will help customers prepare and validate product, supplier, classification, origin, FTA, screening, and workflow data so KYG Trade™ implementations can move from discovery to configuration, testing, training, go-live, and post-go-live adoption with discipline and clarity.
The ideal candidate is analytical, detail-oriented, customer-facing, and comfortable working with messy enterprise data, implementation templates, system exports, workflow outputs, user analytics, and cross-functional project teams. This person should be able to translate data findings into clear customer-ready summaries, identify risks before they become blockers, and support implementation teams with practical execution.
What You’ll Do ·   Support customer onboarding and implementation workstreams by analyzing customer product, supplier, BOM, classification, origin, FTA, screening, and workflow data for completeness, quality, consistency, and readiness.
·   Partner with Customer Success Project Managers, Implementation Leads, Solution Architects, trade SMEs, Product, Engineering, AI, and customers to define data requirements, templates, mapping needs, validation rules, and acceptance criteria.
·   Prepare, clean, transform, compare, and validate customer data sets for platform configuration, migration, testing, workflow setup, AI-assisted classification, FTA qualification, supplier solicitation, restricted party screening, and reporting use cases.
·   Create customer-ready analysis outputs including data readiness summaries, validation trackers, issue logs, user analytics reports, classification progress reports, attestation summaries, adoption metrics, and executive-friendly status views.
·   Assist with platform configuration and implementation setup activities, including customer data uploads, user/workflow setup support, LOV/reference data review, test data preparation, and coordination of environment readiness.
·   Support user acceptance testing by preparing test data, tracking defects or configuration gaps, validating expected outcomes, documenting findings, and coordinating follow-up with internal teams.
·   Help customers understand data dependencies and downstream operational impacts by explaining how data quality affects classification, FTA/origin analysis, screening, supplier engagement, audit records, and reporting outcomes.
·   Participate in customer workshops, office hours, trainings, and implementation meetings to capture data-related requirements, clarify open questions, and provide practical guidance to customer stakeholders.
·   Track data-related risks and blockers across implementations, escalate issues early, and help maintain RAID logs, action trackers, and implementation status materials.
·   Develop reusable templates, checklists, data dictionaries, validation methods, reporting formats, and playbooks that improve implementation speed, quality, and repeatability.
·   Support internal CS execution by maintaining account-level analytics, customer usage insights, onboarding metrics, implementation dashboards, and operational reporting as needed.
·   Collaborate with Product and Engineering to document data issues, workflow defects, reporting gaps, customer enhancement requests, and recurring implementation pain points.
·   Operate with high attention to detail and a strong customer-service orientation, ensuring deliverables are clear, accurate, timely, and ready for customer or leadership review.
What We’re Looking For ·   2+ years of experience in data analysis, SaaS implementation, customer success operations, business analysis, project coordination, supply chain operations, trade compliance, or adjacent analytical/customer-facing roles.
·   Strong Excel and data manipulation skills, including comfort with CSV/XLSX files, lookups, pivots, formulas, data cleansing, deduplication, reconciliation, and structured validation workflows.
·   Ability to analyze incomplete or inconsistent customer data and translate findings into clear risks, requirements, next steps, and customer-facing recommendations.
·   Experience supporting software implementations, onboarding projects, data migrations, system configuration, UAT, workflow testing, reporting, or operational process improvement.
·   Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain data issues and implementation dependencies to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
·   Comfort working directly with customers in workshops, office hours, data reviews, training sessions, and implementation touchpoints.
·   Strong organizational discipline, including comfort maintaining trackers, status reports, issue logs, validation notes, meeting follow-ups, and implementation documentation.
·   Ability to work cross-functionally with Customer Success, Project Management, Product, Engineering, AI, Managed Services, Sales, and trade SMEs in a fast-moving environment.
·   Interest in global trade, customs compliance, product classification, origin/FTA, supplier engagement, restricted party screening, tariff management, ESG traceability, or supply chain data.
·   Preferred: Experience with SQL, BI/reporting tools, Python, data visualization, SaaS analytics, ERP/PLM exports, product master data, BOM data, or supplier data.
·   Preferred: Experience in global trade management technology, customs brokerage, trade consulting, supply chain software, regulatory technology, or enterprise SaaS implementation.
·   Preferred: Familiarity with AI-enabled workflows, human-in-the-loop review, data enrichment, structured prompts, knowledge-base development, or customer adoption analytics.
Why KYG Trade™ ·    Category-defining platform:
Help deliver a modern, AI-native GTM solution in a market shaped by rising tariff complexity, customs scrutiny, forced labor enforcement, supply chain disruption, and increasing demand for automation.
·    High-impact customer work:
Support customer implementations and onboarding motions that directly improve compliance outcomes, operational efficiency, audit readiness, and time-to-value.
·    Cross-functional influence:
Work closely with Customer Success, Implementation, Product, Engineering, AI, Managed Services, Sales, and trade subject matter experts to improve delivery quality and customer outcomes.
·    Builder’s environment:
Help define repeatable playbooks, templates, reporting standards, onboarding models, and customer-facing delivery practices as KYG Trade™ scales.
·    Remote-first culture:
Join a distributed team with strong domain expertise, practical collaboration, and opportunities to grow with the business.
Compensation & Metrics ·    Compensation:
Competitive base salary, bonus eligibility, and equity participation aligned to experience and impact.
·    Implementation support metrics:
Data readiness, quality of validation outputs, speed and accuracy of implementation support, timely issue identification, and customer-facing deliverable quality.
·    Customer success metrics:
Adoption support, training readiness, stakeholder satisfaction, customer usage visibility, and contribution to successful onboarding and go-live outcomes.
·    Operational metrics:
Strong documentation, disciplined trackers, accurate reporting, proactive risk escalation, and repeatable data/process templates.
·    Business impact:
Help customers accelerate time-to-value by ensuring their data, workflows, and implementation activities are structured, validated, and ready for execution on KYG Trade™.
Hiring Process ·    Intro call:

·    Cross-functional interviews:

·    Practical scenario or working session:

·    References + offer:
We aim to move efficiently once there is mutual alignment and provide clear communication throughout the process.
If you combine analytical rigor, customer-facing execution, and a builder’s mindset for scaling SaaS implementation quality, we’d love to hear from you.

Who We Are

AMPAM is the leading design-build Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) contractor serving large-scale multifamily and commercial projects across California. With 1,500 employees across multiple business units, we are committed to delivering quality, safety, and excellence in every project.

Job Summary

The Project Coordinator (PC) supports project management teams in the planning, documentation, and execution of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) construction projects. This role ensures the timely flow of information between the field, office, vendors, and clients—supporting operational efficiency, cost control, and quality delivery across all active projects.

Key Responsibilities Include:
(But not limited to the following)

Assist Project Managers and Superintendents in coordinating day-to-day project activities and schedules.
Prepare, track, and manage project documentation including RFIs, submittals, meeting minutes, and change orders.
Maintain accurate and organized project files within company systems (e.g., Procore, Bluebeam, Spectrum, etc.).
Support project cost tracking, invoice processing, and purchase order management.
Monitor material orders and delivery schedules in coordination with procurement and field teams.
Facilitate internal and external communication between field operations, subcontractors, and clients.
Prepare project status reports and distribute weekly updates to leadership as required.
Assist with job closeout documentation, warranty tracking, and project archiving.
Partner with Payroll and HRIS teams as needed for project-specific labor or timekeeping reconciliations.
Ensure adherence to company safety, quality, and compliance standards.

Qualifications

Technical Skills:
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams).
Experience using construction management software (Procore, Bluebeam, Spectrum or similar).
Familiarity with reading and understanding construction drawings and specifications.
Competencies:
Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Collaborative mindset and customer service orientation.
Ability to adapt in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

Preferred

Watershed Scientist & Program Manager

The Glen Lake Association (GLA) is seeking a passionate and collaborative Watershed Scientist & Program Manager to lead our science and stewardship efforts in the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed. This is a rare opportunity to build a meaningful career protecting one of Michigan's most treasured freshwater ecosystems while working alongside talented colleagues, engaged volunteers, and a community that deeply values conservation.

Position Summary

The Watershed Scientist & Program Manager serves as the GLA's scientific leader, advancing the understanding and long-term stewardship of the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed in Leelanau County, Michigan. This position offers a unique opportunity to combine hands-on field science with community engagement in one of Michigan's most treasured freshwater systems. 

You'll oversee the GLA's water quality, watershed science, and invasive species programs while communicating science in ways that inspire informed decision-making and stewardship. Working closely with the Executive Director, you'll lead seasonal staff, interns, volunteers, and program partners to deliver impactful science and stewardship initiatives. 

The ideal candidate is a collaborative scientist who enjoys spending time in the field, mentoring others, building partnerships, and making complex science accessible to the community.

Watershed Program Leadership

Develop annual work plans and lead the day-to-day management of the GLA's water quality, invasive species, stewardship, and scientific monitoring programs. 
Monitor program progress, budgets, and key deliverables. 
Supervise and mentor seasonal staff, interns, volunteers, and contractors.
Contribute scientific expertise to organizational strategic planning and long-term program development. 
Prepare technical reports, annual summaries, and scientific content to support organizational communications and decision-making. 
Partner with the Executive Director to identify funding opportunities and provide technical expertise for grant proposals and applications. 
Recommend, where appropriate, new monitoring initiatives and scientific approaches to address emerging watershed issues.

Science, Monitoring, & Management

Lead and oversee long-term monitoring of water quality and watershed conditions. 
Conduct and supervise watershed monitoring using a variety of scientific field methods and equipment, including water quality sampling with multi-probe sondes; shoreline assessments; aquatic vegetation surveys conducted through snorkeling or scuba; and the use of drones, remotely operated vehicles, and microscopes.  
Monitor and interpret biological indicators of watershed health, including aquatic vegetation, plankton communities, fisheries data, wildlife observations, and other ecological trends. 
Lead implementation of aquatic and terrestrial invasive species prevention, early detection, and response efforts. 
Manage long-term datasets and ensure data quality and reporting. 
Analyze and interpret data to identify trends and management opportunities.

Community Science, Stewardship, & Education

Lead the GLA's stewardship and community science programs, including the Guardian Stewardship and Discovery Boat programs. 
Design meaningful internship experiences and oversee, mentor, and support interns engaged in watershed science. 
Recruit and train volunteers participating in citizen science initiatives and stewardship programs.  
Represent the GLA through outreach and public presentations that communicate science and inspire stewardship.

Partnerships & Scientific Collaboration

Develop and maintain partnerships with government and tribal agencies, researchers, nonprofits, and other watershed organizations. 
Serve as the staff liaison and scientific advisor to the GLA Water Quality Committee.

Equipment & Assets  

Oversee the operation, maintenance, calibration, and replacement planning for scientific equipment, boats, trailers, and other assets. 
Support the Water Levels Committee in coordinating dam operations and required inspections while monitoring compliance with the court order and applicable permits and regulations.

Qualifications

Required 

Bachelor's degree in Limnology, Environmental Science, Ecology, Natural Resources Management, or a related field. 
Five or more years of progressively responsible professional experience in watershed science, aquatic ecology, environmental management, or a related field, including experience leading conservation or natural resource programs. 
Demonstrated experience managing teams and/or volunteers. 
Strong project management, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to balance multiple priorities and meet deadlines. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate scientific information effectively to a variety of audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build collaborative relationships with partners, volunteers, agencies, and community. 
Experience using Microsoft Office and GIS or spatial mapping software, with the ability to learn emerging technologies. 
Experience operating boats, conducting fieldwork safely in aquatic environments, and swimming. 
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
Must reside year-round within Benzie, Leelanau, or Grand Traverse County.

Preferred 

Master’s degree in related field
Experience with freshwater science and management. 
Experience using drones, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), or remote sensing technologies. 
Experience communicating scientific information to community audiences or leading environmental education programs.

Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered. Research shows many qualified candidates, particularly women and underrepresented groups, hesitate to apply unless their experience aligns perfectly. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply.

Working Conditions & Physical Demands

This hybrid position is based out of the GLA's office at 6406 Western Ave., Glen Arbor, MI 49636, with work-from-home flexibility in the off-season. Substantial time is spent outdoors on or near the water. Responsibilities include operating boats, carrying equipment, hiking uneven terrain, and swimming. Work may involve exposure to heat, cold, rain, wind, and other environmental conditions. Office responsibilities require sitting and repetitive computer use.

Compensation 

The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $75,000, commensurate with experience. Benefits include a flexible hybrid work schedule, vacation time, sick leave, and a health care stipend.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and cover letter to apply@glenlakeassociation.org by September 1, 2026. Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

About the Glen Lake Association 

Founded in 1945, the Glen Lake Association (GLA) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to preserving the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed. Through science-based programs, strategic partnerships, and community stewardship, the GLA works to safeguard water quality and natural resources across the watershed. Located within and adjacent to Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, this watershed is one of Michigan's natural treasures, where pristine lakes and streams support a vibrant ecosystem. The GLA enjoys an engaged community of residents, visitors, and business owners who are committed to protecting water quality now and for generations. 

A Day in the Life at the GLA

The Water Investment Division's Clean Water Initiative Program (CWIP) is seeking a highly motivated individual who is knowledgeable and passionate about clean water with technical, organizational, and communications skills. The Lake Champlain Basin Program (LCBP) partnership is an important component of the state's ongoing efforts to reduce pollution and restore and protect ecosystem health in the Lake Champlain basin. The LCBP Grants Manager position leads management, monitoring, and reporting of federal grants awarded to the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under the supervision of the Vermont Coordinator. This position works as part of CWIP's team focused on grant administration, operational support, funding initiative design, and implementation and works collaboratively to respond to emerging continuous improvement, accessible communications, and Vermont's Environmental Justice Law priorities. This position may include potential to telework.

Support the Vermont Coordinator in preparing the annual grant application. Lead programmatic financial tracking in partnership with DEC Federal Financial Manager to ensure spending is aligned with workplans.

Operational Support (~25%)
: Lead LCBP program operations to advance several dynamic projects. Use and improve tracking systems to accurately monitor programmatic and financial status of projects. The Center for Ecoliteracy is seeking a Communications and Program Coordinator to join our small and dynamic team that includes educators, former school nutrition professionals, food systems experts, advocates, and parents.

About this Role

The Communications and Program Coordinator supports the organization’s mission by coordinating program activities and translating those efforts into compelling digital communications that engage participants, partners, and broader audiences. 

This is a key role on our team that will advance the Center for Ecoliteracy’s California Food for California Kids® initiative. The Communications and Program Coordinator will build relationships with school nutrition leaders across California, help shape the statewide conversation on transforming school food, experience and document stories of innovative farm to school programs, and contribute to policy and systems change that benefits millions of students.

This position reports to the Program Manager of the California Food for California Kids® initiative and is a full-time, exempt position. 

Who We Are Seeking 

You are a thoughtful communicator with a collaborative spirit. You keep a pulse on new communications platforms and technology. Meeting new people and picking up the phone gives you energy and inspiration. You prioritize authentic relationships over outcomes. You enjoy translating complex ideas into clear, engaging content and are skilled at managing multiple projects and platforms. Technology is your friend – you’re a problem-solver when it comes to tech glitches and hiccups. You are excited to support a mission-driven team working to create a more equitable and sustainable school food system. You love food and the culture surrounding it, with a deep appreciation for the people who grow and prepare it, as well as the community they serve. You are proactive, detail-oriented, and ready to dive in and contribute meaningfully to a small, high-impact organization.

Our Workplace Culture

The Center for Ecoliteracy supports a culture that prioritizes integrity, high professional standards, and working successfully with diverse colleagues, program beneficiaries, and community partners. This includes active participation in promoting a healthy workplace culture through organizational diversity and program assessment for equity and inclusion. We strive to build a culture of cooperation and mutual support and value flexibility, resilience, optimism, curiosity, and a sense of shared purpose.

Responsibilities

Lead digital communications across video, websites, webinars, email campaigns, and social media platforms. Generate compelling content, including short-form videos, graphics, and photography that engage program beneficiaries, donors, and partners.
Support the development of comprehensive communication plans to effectively disseminate new resources, event opportunities, and other program offerings. Liaise with partner organizations to coordinate cross-promotion and resource dissemination.
Support the coordination of photo and video shoots at schools, farms, and events throughout California. Provide on-site support for vendors and program participants to ensure a positive, meaningful experience.
Track and analyze digital metrics to inform communication strategies.
Maintain a brand asset library (graphics, photos, and video), and support the team in using assets correctly.
Support our programs by hosting and facilitating conferences, events, and webinars; coordinating event logistics; and managing outreach, recruitment, promotion, registration, and contact lists. Conduct research and develop prep materials to provide a seamless experience for staff and participants.
Contribute to program evaluation and reporting by gathering data and tracking project outcomes. Lead systems for tracking and managing relationships with school nutrition professionals and educators. 
Represent the organization and engage with school nutrition professionals, educators, students, policymakers, and nonprofit and state agency partners at conferences, events, webinars, and visits to schools and farms.

Minimum 2–3 years of experience in communications, marketing, journalism, or a related field.
Excellent project management skills. Thrives managing multiple deadlines in a fast-paced, collaborative environment while delivering a high standard of excellence.
Experience with event planning and coordination. Comfortable pivoting from detailed execution to strategic decision-making under pressure. 
Comfort engaging with external partners and representing the organization.
Ability to build and use spreadsheets to manage program data, synthesize project outcomes, and communicate impact to staff. 
Strong writing and editing skills, with attention to detail and storytelling.
Proficiency in digital platforms, including social media, email marketing tools, and web content management systems. The Center for Ecoliteracy works in an Apple environment and uses Adobe Creative Cloud, Drupal, Mailchimp, Hootsuite, Zoom, Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Threads, Slack, Dropbox, Canva, and Google Workspace.
Proficiency in best practices for digital design, such as editing, cropping, and ensuring correct file types for different platforms.  
Experience tailoring content for various audiences, such as school nutrition professionals, educators, donors, policymakers, or California families.

Preferred Skills and Experience

Experience working with nonprofit organizations or public school nutrition programs.
Familiarity with food systems, education, or advocacy campaigns.
Spanish language fluency is a plus.

Location and Travel

The Center for Ecoliteracy has a hybrid work environment in the landmark David Brower Center in Downtown Berkeley, California. This role follows a hybrid schedule (in-office on Tuesday and Thursday, remote on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday) and requires regular travel to support events, storytelling, and other engagements within California.

Salary

This is a full-time, exempt position. The salary is based on experience and ranges from $80,000 to $85,000 annually. A comprehensive benefits package is included.

Please email a brief cover letter, three relevant work samples, and your resume to jobs@ecoliteracy.org with the subject line “[Last Name, First Name]: Communications and Program Coordinator Application.” Interviews will be conducted in August 2026.

The Center for Ecoliteracy is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, or disability.

Our Commitment to Equity and Racial Justice

The Center for Ecoliteracy pursues change in TK–12 education and school food systems to provide a more just, sustainable, and equitable experience for students and the people who nourish them. We recognize the harm that systemic racism, gender bias, and structural inequalities create in our public education, food, and labor systems, and strive to mitigate the health and educational inequities affecting low-income households and children of color. By listening and taking action to identify and include missing voices, we seek to shift power in both policy and decision-making. We are privileged to learn from our partners and will continue to grow and evolve our work to embody this commitment.

The Center for Ecoliteracy is reimagining school food as a pathway for learning and change.
For 30 years, we’ve transformed education in classrooms, cafeterias, and gardens—partnering with hundreds of school districts, supporting thousands of educators, and ensuring millions of children have access to nutritious meals at school.

Watershed Scientist & Program Manager

The Glen Lake Association (GLA) is seeking a passionate and collaborative Watershed Scientist & Program Manager to lead our science and stewardship efforts in the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed. This is a rare opportunity to build a meaningful career protecting one of Michigan's most treasured freshwater ecosystems while working alongside talented colleagues, engaged volunteers, and a community that deeply values conservation.

Position Summary

The Watershed Scientist & Program Manager serves as the GLA's scientific leader, advancing the understanding and long-term stewardship of the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed in Leelanau County, Michigan. This position offers a unique opportunity to combine hands-on field science with community engagement in one of Michigan's most treasured freshwater systems. 

You'll oversee the GLA's water quality, watershed science, and invasive species programs while communicating science in ways that inspire informed decision-making and stewardship. Working closely with the Executive Director, you'll lead seasonal staff, interns, volunteers, and program partners to deliver impactful science and stewardship initiatives. 

The ideal candidate is a collaborative scientist who enjoys spending time in the field, mentoring others, building partnerships, and making complex science accessible to the community.

Watershed Program Leadership

Develop annual work plans and lead the day-to-day management of the GLA's water quality, invasive species, stewardship, and scientific monitoring programs. 
Monitor program progress, budgets, and key deliverables. 
Supervise and mentor seasonal staff, interns, volunteers, and contractors.
Contribute scientific expertise to organizational strategic planning and long-term program development. 
Prepare technical reports, annual summaries, and scientific content to support organizational communications and decision-making. 
Partner with the Executive Director to identify funding opportunities and provide technical expertise for grant proposals and applications. 
Recommend, where appropriate, new monitoring initiatives and scientific approaches to address emerging watershed issues.

Science, Monitoring, & Management

Lead and oversee long-term monitoring of water quality and watershed conditions. 
Conduct and supervise watershed monitoring using a variety of scientific field methods and equipment, including water quality sampling with multi-probe sondes; shoreline assessments; aquatic vegetation surveys conducted through snorkeling or scuba; and the use of drones, remotely operated vehicles, and microscopes.  
Monitor and interpret biological indicators of watershed health, including aquatic vegetation, plankton communities, fisheries data, wildlife observations, and other ecological trends. 
Lead implementation of aquatic and terrestrial invasive species prevention, early detection, and response efforts. 
Manage long-term datasets and ensure data quality and reporting. 
Analyze and interpret data to identify trends and management opportunities.

Community Science, Stewardship, & Education

Lead the GLA's stewardship and community science programs, including the Guardian Stewardship and Discovery Boat programs. 
Design meaningful internship experiences and oversee, mentor, and support interns engaged in watershed science. 
Recruit and train volunteers participating in citizen science initiatives and stewardship programs.  
Represent the GLA through outreach and public presentations that communicate science and inspire stewardship.

Partnerships & Scientific Collaboration

Develop and maintain partnerships with government and tribal agencies, researchers, nonprofits, and other watershed organizations. 
Serve as the staff liaison and scientific advisor to the GLA Water Quality Committee.

Equipment & Assets  

Oversee the operation, maintenance, calibration, and replacement planning for scientific equipment, boats, trailers, and other assets. 
Support the Water Levels Committee in coordinating dam operations and required inspections while monitoring compliance with the court order and applicable permits and regulations.

Qualifications

Required 

Bachelor's degree in Limnology, Environmental Science, Ecology, Natural Resources Management, or a related field. 
Five or more years of progressively responsible professional experience in watershed science, aquatic ecology, environmental management, or a related field, including experience leading conservation or natural resource programs. 
Demonstrated experience managing teams and/or volunteers. 
Strong project management, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to balance multiple priorities and meet deadlines. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate scientific information effectively to a variety of audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build collaborative relationships with partners, volunteers, agencies, and community. 
Experience using Microsoft Office and GIS or spatial mapping software, with the ability to learn emerging technologies. 
Experience operating boats, conducting fieldwork safely in aquatic environments, and swimming. 
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
Must reside year-round within Benzie, Leelanau, or Grand Traverse County.

Preferred 

Master’s degree in related field
Experience with freshwater science and management. 
Experience using drones, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), or remote sensing technologies. 
Experience communicating scientific information to community audiences or leading environmental education programs.

Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered. Research shows many qualified candidates, particularly women and underrepresented groups, hesitate to apply unless their experience aligns perfectly. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply.

Working Conditions & Physical Demands

This hybrid position is based out of the GLA's office at 6406 Western Ave., Glen Arbor, MI 49636, with work-from-home flexibility in the off-season. Substantial time is spent outdoors on or near the water. Responsibilities include operating boats, carrying equipment, hiking uneven terrain, and swimming. Work may involve exposure to heat, cold, rain, wind, and other environmental conditions. Office responsibilities require sitting and repetitive computer use.

Compensation 

The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $75,000, commensurate with experience. Benefits include a flexible hybrid work schedule, vacation time, sick leave, and a health care stipend.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and cover letter to apply@glenlakeassociation.org by September 1, 2026. Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

About the Glen Lake Association 

Founded in 1945, the Glen Lake Association (GLA) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to preserving the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed. Through science-based programs, strategic partnerships, and community stewardship, the GLA works to safeguard water quality and natural resources across the watershed. Located within and adjacent to Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, this watershed is one of Michigan's natural treasures, where pristine lakes and streams support a vibrant ecosystem. The GLA enjoys an engaged community of residents, visitors, and business owners who are committed to protecting water quality now and for generations. 

A Day in the Life at the GLA 

At the GLA, no two days are the same. One day you might be collecting water quality data by boat or conducting snorkel surveys for aquatic vegetation. The next, you may be sharing scientific findings with the community at the local library or collaborating in a conservation partner's office to help shape the future of watershed protection.  

This is mission-driven work with a tangible impact. Every project and conversation contributes to protecting the health of the Glen Lake/Crystal River Watershed for future generations. If you’re passionate about freshwater science, enjoy working on the water, thrive in a collaborative environment, and want your expertise to directly support the stewardship of one of Michigan’s most treasured freshwater systems, you’ll feel right at home at the GLA.
